why: Every source needs one safe, repeatable way in, so a failing or missing source never stops the product.
The same person appears in the CRM, email, LinkedIn and data providers. Without one record, signals and sends attach to the wrong person.
Every agent must read the same history before it acts and write back after. This memory is what compounds, and it is what the customer owns.
A signal that is months old must stop counting, or old news keeps ranking accounts.
Contacting a customer, a competitor or someone who opted out is the costliest mistake, so this check comes before everything else.
A rep, and the AI, must see one account's whole story from first touch to today.
Any rank or action must be explainable later, with the evidence and the rules in force that day.
Outcomes only teach the system if every send is logged with its exact cause.
Messages and assets must be grounded in the customer's own documents and cite them, so nothing is invented.
Reps should ask, decide and act in one conversation, not across screens.
Nothing should reach reps until it has been tested on cases where the answer is already known.

feature: Versioned prompts, rules and cost logging
why: Prompts and rules change. Every change must be versioned, costed and reversible.
Lessons from lost deals and objections must be stored so the system can use them later.
When the AI cannot decide, a named person must get the item with a reason, a deadline and a default.
Each customer needs its own setup. Reaching a first ranked queue in four weeks depends on setup being configuration, not code.
Different people need different access, and one customer's data must never mix with another's.
The customer may or may not know their ICP. Either way a confirmed ICP is needed to start.
The confirmed ICP must turn into a list of real candidate accounts and contacts.
No single data provider is complete. Trying the cheapest first controls cost.
Providers can disagree. Each record needs a trust level so doubtful ones are not used blindly.
Only accounts that fit should be paid for, so fit is judged on free attributes first.
The list must not contain existing customers or open deals.
Reps need verified contact details and company facts, paid for only when an account fits.
The next stages need the whole list and everything collected, not a summary.
Doubtful records must not vanish or pass silently. They are held, retried, then given to a person.
People change jobs and emails. Stored records must stay right without good data being overwritten by errors.
The team must see where data coverage is thin so the waterfall can be widened.
Every signal type needs a defined source, level, tier and window in one place.
Signals must be fetched for each target account on a schedule.
A whole sector moving (rules, energy, news) changes timing for many accounts at once.
Events at an account (tenders, funding, hiring) are the clearest evidence of timing.
An account committed to a rival, or one that is weakening, is a reason to act now.
A new executive, or a champion's move, is a reason to reach a person now.
How accounts engage with us (website, content, email) shows interest.
Replies, LinkedIn threads and call notes contain dates and next steps.
CRM activity shows a known contact resurfacing or a new contact appearing.
A personal connection makes outreach warmer and more likely to work.
Buyers now research through AI assistants, and that traffic is intent.
A late or repeated signal should weigh less than a fresh first one.
Only signals that are verifiable, predictive and time-bound should count.
Two events of the same type are not equally strong. The content decides.
Signals fade at different speeds. The tier sets the points and the decay.
A signal that no longer applies (a champion moved) must be removed, and each signal tied to the right persona.
Some signals (a positive reply, a live demo) need action in minutes, not the next morning.
A signal far outside its normal range may be a real event worth an alert.
New signals should earn weight from results, and sources that fail should be flagged.
The list of signals must keep growing as gaps and anomalies appear.
Comments, likes and shares on LinkedIn show interest, but only if the content shows the interest is relevant.
Reps need to know how well an account matches the ICP.
Timing must reflect how many live signals there are, and how fresh and strong they are.
Ranking by fit times timing puts accounts that fit and are ready first. A good fit with nothing happening ranks zero.
A rank needs a one-line reason and an honest confidence.
Scoring must be proven on known won and lost accounts before reps rely on it.
Scoring rules should be drafted from the customer's own won deals and be readable.
Big accounts always have signals, so each account should be compared with its own normal.
Weights should be re-learned from outcomes.
Messages and plays must fit the customer's niche, not only the industry.
What triggered the account decides the angle of the message.
The message depends on who is being contacted.
Nothing may be routed to an excluded account, or one touched recently.
Selling to a committee needs the right set of people.
The framing depends on whether buyers care about growth or cost.
A group sharing a trigger is best worked as one campaign. A rule decides when.
What worked per segment should shape the next plays.
Two reps must not work the same live opportunity, and history must inform the message.
A warm path changes the channel and the odds.
Reps need to know the moment someone else engages, an account closes or a champion moves.
Messages need a proven structure. Until one is proven, the draft is marked unproven.
A rep needs one decided action: who, what, channel, why now, with the evidence.
The channel should be chosen from verified data and from what has worked.
Nothing unsupported or off-brand should go out.
The AI should decide what it can and give a person only what it cannot.
A person decides the items that fail a criterion, and every campaign.
Reps start the day with a ranked list of what changed and what to do.
A trigger shared by many accounts is worth one coordinated three-touch campaign.
Repeatable outreach needs versioned plays.
The list must re-order the moment something happens.
Work must go to the right team by territory, product or deal size.
Actions must reach reps where they work.
The system should reuse what is proven and keep testing alternatives.
Writers and checkers need one source of voice, tone, approved claims and banned phrases.
Assets (decks, one-pagers) must be made in the customer's brand without us building a design tool.
Different steps need different formats.
Assets must be grounded, cited and checked before use.
Outreach should open with why the account fits, and cite sources.
Past campaigns should become experience for the next one.
Questions the library cannot answer show what content is missing.
An asset should be swappable in a live campaign.
Rep edits show what good looks like, so the system should learn from them.
Repeated narrow jobs should run on small, cheap models.

feature: Interim sending via the rep's mailbox
why: Until integrated sending exists, reps send from their own mailbox, and the system must still capture each send.
The system must enforce who approves what, and when the AI may send alone.
A person must never be hit on three channels in 48 hours.
Sends should run through the tools the customer already uses.
Customer teams should be able to run campaigns themselves by connecting their tools.
Follow-up should continue until there is a clear answer.
Every reply must be saved against its account.
Each reply needs a status and a default next step.
We must know which signal and message started each conversation.
Someone who looked but did not reply is a warm lead.
Which reply beat which objection should improve future replies.
Every decision must be logged, and today's numbers recorded as the baseline.
Outcomes, hits and misses alike, are what the system learns from.

feature: Funnel per 100 and prioritised vs the rest
why: Results must be compared fairly: per 100 accounts, and prioritised against the rest.
Rep, manager and leader each need their own numbers.
The customer pays per qualified meeting, so the definition must be tracked.
The system should improve every month without a bigger model.
Each channel should be checked against an outside benchmark.
A person should review learned changes before they ship.
A leader needs the gap to quota and a plan to close it.
We need to know why customers in the category buy, and what they cite.

feature: Rival detection, review reading and matching
why: What a rival's customers complain about is the angle for our message.
Complaint themes should be tested against replies, per segment.
The customer's own won conversations hold patterns worth mining.

feature: Who replied, and what to write
why: A rep's first question each morning is who replied and what to write.

feature: Who has not replied but looked
why: Someone who looked but did not reply is worth a second touch.
Managers and reps need to see which step of a campaign is weak and what to change.
A rep needs one account's whole history before a call.
A meeting needs a brief, a deck and the missing stakeholders found.

feature: Follow up on this week's demos
why: After a demo the follow-up, gaps and risks must be captured the same day.

feature: How far am I from quota
why: A rep needs to know how far they are from quota and what to do about it.
The customer's CRM stays the record. We read it so we never contact customers or open deals, and we never write to it.
Sends, replies and meetings live in email and calendar.
Reps work in Slack and need alerts and actions there.
Reps work in Teams and need alerts and actions there.
Power users and operations want a command line.
The customer's own tools and other agents should be able to call our reasoning layer.
Our agents should be able to use the tools the customer has already connected.
First-party events (web, marketing) are signals.
Conversations and LinkedIn views are signals.
Customers want the data in their own BI tools.
